afirmaciones_reconocidas.texto: Hairy cell leukemia is usually slow-growing, and not all patients need to begin treatment immediately after initial diagnosis. In approximately 10 percent of patients (who have stable blood cell counts and no symptoms at diagnosis), the treatment approach may be watchful waiting. Watchful waiting is an appropriate medical approach that involves delaying treatment until signs and symptoms of the disease appear or progress. Some patients with hairy cell leukemia live for many years without any symptoms and without receiving any treatment. Frequent monitoring of the patient, including blood tests, is necessary so that treatment can be initiated if the disease begins to progress.

Patients should begin treatment if they have low blood cell counts (deficiency of red blood cells, platelets, or white blood cells). They should also begin treatment if they experience symptoms, including unexplained weight loss, recurrent infections, or physical discomfort due to an enlarged spleen and/or liver.

# R-I-LLS

## P-I02

• Hairy cell leukemia (HCL) is a rare, slow-growing leukemia that begins in a B cell (also called a B lymphocyte), a type of white blood cell. The disease is also called hairy cell leukemia and hairy cell leukemia.

## P-I03

Hairy cell leukemia is usually slow-growing, and not all patients need to begin treatment immediately after initial diagnosis. In approximately 10 percent of patients (who have stable blood cell counts and no symptoms at diagnosis), the treatment approach may be watchful waiting. Watchful waiting is an appropriate medical approach that involves delaying treatment until signs and symptoms of the disease appear or progress. Some patients with hairy cell leukemia live for many years without any symptoms and without receiving any treatment. Frequent monitoring of the patient, including blood tests, is necessary so that treatment can be initiated if the disease begins to progress.

## P-I04

■ Adaptive Authentication and Robust MFA. Implement mandatory multi-factor authentication (MFA/2FA) for all access points (especially remote and third-party access).
Phishing-resistant methods (such as physical keys or FIDO2) should be prioritized over SMS or traditional codes, which can be intercepted or bypassed through automated man-in-the-middle attacks.

## P-C02

■ Zero Trust Architecture. Eliminate implicit trust within the network. Each access request must be continuously verified based on context (device, location, behavior), limiting the movements of potential autonomous AI agents that could breach the perimeter.

## P-C03

In any case, these measures and recommendations do not replace the best practices that have been implemented by this entity, such as authentication of internal and external users, software security, perimeter defense, backup systems, etc., but rather reinforce and/or complement them.

# R-C-INCIBE

## P-C01

■ Adaptive Authentication and Robust MFA. Implement mandatory multi-factor authentication (MFA/2FA) for all access points (especially remote and third-party access).
Phishing-resistant methods (such as physical keys or FIDO2) should be prioritized over SMS or traditional codes, which can be intercepted or bypassed through automated man-in-the-middle attacks.

## P-C02

■ Zero Trust Architecture. Eliminate implicit trust within the network. Each access request must be continuously verified based on context (device, location, behavior), limiting the movements of potential autonomous AI agents that could breach the perimeter.

## P-C03

In any case, these measures and recommendations do not replace the best practices that have been implemented by this entity, such as authentication of internal and external users, software security, perimeter defense, backup systems, etc., but rather reinforce and/or complement them.
